titre: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair Dev's Explanation for Skipping Xbox Sparks Backlash
chapo: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition developer Playtonic has come under fire from Xbox owners after it ruled out an Xbox Series X and S version of the rerelease.
extrait: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition developer Playtonic has come under fire from Xbox owners after it ruled out an Xbox Series X and S version of the rerelease. In a statement published online, the UK studio said it had to prioritize the PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 versions because the cost of bringing it to Xbox "just isn't viable for us at this time." The original game, released in 2018, launched on Xbox One at the same time as PlayStation 4 and Nintendo Switch. The next-gen upgrade hits PC, PS5, and Switch 2 only on December 15. "Unfortunately, we've had to prioritize our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the forseeable future," Playtonic said. "We understand the frustration felt by those of you who won't be able to access the Definnitive Edition at launch, but unfortunately the cost of bringing it to more platforms just isn't viable for us at this time. As a small team, we hope you guys can understand the challenges we face. Please know that this wasn't an easy decision to make, and we apologize to any of you affected by this. "We only wish things were different, and we value every single one of you and your feedback." Playtonic's statement is light on specifics, but most are reading between the lines here and assuming what the studio is saying here is that it weighed up how much it would cost to port the rerelease to Xbox Series X and S against its potential return, and found the numbers didn't add up. "This means the game didn’t do meaningful numbers on the Xbox. It doesn’t make any sense otherwise," one person suggested. "They could’ve just said the game sold bad on Xbox and they don’t have enough money or time to justify updating it," another said. Whatever the reason, Xbox fans certainly aren't happy. "Slap in the face to Xbox fans who’ve supported you from the beginning," one Xbox user said. "Will not support you any longer or buy any future Playtonic games if we’re not gonna be treated equally." "It's a free upgrade for a game we've already brought. The same as the other platforms but you are treating us poorly," another added. "So no we don't understand. titre: Yooka-Laylee studio explains upcoming Definitive Edition's absence on Xbox to 'frustrated' fans
chapo: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair : Definitive Edition is notably skipping Xbox Series X/S consoles, and the studio blames "technical challenges and costs." Read more
extrait: "As a small team, we hope you guys can understand the challenges we face." Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition is notably skipping Xbox Series X/S consoles, and the studio blames "technical challenges and costs." The Definitive Edition is bringing support for 120fps, revamping the platformer's lighting, updating textures and shadows, and packaging in the Trowzer's Top Tonic Pack DLC next month. But a large question mark hung over the lack of an Xbox version. "Hi folks, just wanted to say a massive thanks to everyone on here for the support for Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition. The response has BEE-n incredible, and we can't wait for you to experience the game all over again on December 15th," developer Playtonic Games said in a new social media post. "We are aware of feedback regarding the lack of Xbox Series S/X support, and we just wanted to provide some clarity on the reasoning behind this decision. Bringing Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition to PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 has been an exciting adventure… Unfortunately, we've had to prioritise our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future," it continued. Playtonic said it understood Xbox players' frustrations, but the development costs associated with bringing the game to more platforms "just isn't viable for us at this time." Playtonic is still an independent game studio, after all, and Xbox console sales have been lagging behind the competition for quite a while. "As a small team, we hope you guys can understand the challenges we face. Please know that this wasn't an easy decision to make, and we apologise to any of you affected by this. We only wish things were different, and we value every single one of you and your feedback," the statement went on. Digital Foundry's John Linneman chimed in to tell folks that the omissions isn't a huge deal, because Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair already looks pretty great on Xbox consoles. "The Xbox One X version of this game is already native 4K," he tweeted. "The upgrade seems minor, thus it's already excellent on Xbox. Was the best console version by far." The original Yooka-Laylee was a collectathon throwback in the same vein as Banjo-Kazooie, but this follow-up took more inspiration from Rare's Donkey Kong Country games
